title: Author deletes a memory while the partner is reading it
preconditions: A authored a memory that B has opened.
A deletes it from their own device.
B refreshes or navigates back to the memory.
expected_behavior: Only the author can delete the memory.
B no longer sees it after refresh; an already-open detail reports that it is unavailable.
The deletion does not affect B's ability to read other shared memories.
candidate_failure_modes: B can still edit or delete A's memory.
The open detail shows stale content indefinitely or crashes.
Deleting the memory deletes unrelated media still used elsewhere.

observed_code_behavior: Memory create is idempotent per (space_id, client_id) while the row is live.
Update and delete compare the observed updatedAt; a stale write returns 409 without side effects.
Authorship and authorName are computed per viewer, not stored as a snapshot.

hypothetical_user_behavior:
A fictional participant (Mina Sol) said: "Did the walkthrough with VoiceOver on, large text on. Answering in the spirit of the ask: remove, don't redesign.

1) The storage meter. Gone. As a sighted-by-graph element it has no accessible name and no threshold until you're already past it — it tells me a number I cannot act on, and it announces "0 percent" at full. What breaks if removed: nothing. Nobody has ever chosen a plan from that bar. Cost: every launch it makes me re-check whether storage is actually a limit or just decoration.

2) "Manage subscription" as a second heading at the same level as "Plan." Remove the link and fold the verb into the row label. Right now a heading-level sweep reads "heading level 2, Plan" twice and I have to open both to learn which one holds the action. Cost: duplicate headings are a tax paid at every single read.

3) The upgrade prompt inside a feature gate. If the control looks disabled, it is disabled — so the prompt is telling me the one thing the control already told me, at a volume the control didn't. Remove the prompt, keep the gate, and let the disabled state carry a reason string. "Why does this exist?" It exists because the gate doesn't say why. Fix the gate by deleting its narrator.

The one thing I would keep: the paywall's plain-language line stating what you get in words. It's the only place in Plus and storage that says the cost out loud instead of drawing it. Every other surface is a picture of a decision. That line is the decision.

Removed four things and added zero. That was the whole job."
Mina Sol assumes: a heading is a heading
Mina Sol assumes: a button that looks disabled is disabled
Jules Park assumes: the sky is not the archive
Jules Park assumes: a setting applies immediately
